            "content": "<div align=\"center\">\n\n<br/>\n\n<img src=\"frontend/img/ragbucket.png\" alt=\"RagBucket Logo\" width=\"160\" />\n\n<br/>\n\n# RagBucket\n\n<h3><em>Portable Executable RAG Artifacts for Python</em></h3>\n\n**Build once. Load anywhere. Query forever.**\n\n<br/>\n\n[![PyPI version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/ragbucket?style=for-the-badge&color=FFD700&labelColor=0d0d1a&logo=python&logoColor=FFD700)](https://pypi.org/project/ragbucket/)\n[![Python](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/ragbucket?style=for-the-badge&color=4FC3F7&labelColor=0d0d1a)](https://pypi.org/project/ragbucket/)\n[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-A8FF78?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=0d0d1a)](LICENSE)\n[![PyPI Downloads](https://static.pepy.tech/personalized-badge/ragbucket?period=monthly&units=INTERNATIONAL_SYSTEM&left_color=BLUE&right_color=GREEN&left_text=downloads%2Fmonth)](https://pepy.tech/projects/ragbucket)\n<br/>\n[![Website](https://img.shields.io/badge/Website-ragbucket.vercel.app-c084fc?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=0d0d1a&logo=vercel&logoColor=c084fc)](https://ragbucket.vercel.app)\n[![Blog](https://img.shields.io/badge/BLOG-HASHNODE-2962FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=hashnode&logoColor=white)](https://anikchand.hashnode.dev/why-rag-pipelines-aren-t-portable-building-ragbucket)\n\n<br/>\n\n<p>\n  <a href=\"#-the-problem\">Problem</a> ·\n  <a href=\"#-introducing-rag\">The .rag Format</a> ·\n  <a href=\"#-installation\">Install</a> ·\n  <a href=\"#-quickstart\">Quickstart</a> ·\n  <a href=\"#-multi-provider-runtime\">Providers</a> ·\n  <a href=\"#-roadmap\">Roadmap</a>\n</p>\n\n<br/>\n\n</div>\n\n---\n\n## ◈ The Problem\n\nEvery major ML format is portable by default:\n\n```\nmodel.pt   ·   model.onnx   ·   model.gguf   ·   model.h5\n```\n\nYou save them, share them, deploy them anywhere.\n\n**RAG systems can't do any of that.**\n\nA typical RAG pipeline is a fragile web of moving parts:\n\n```\n❌  Vector databases tied to specific infrastructure\n❌  Embedding pipelines that must be rebuilt from scratch\n❌  Chunking configs scattered across codebases\n❌  Provider-specific integrations with zero portability\n❌  Metadata that lives nowhere and everywhere at once\n```\n\nEvery time you switch environments — laptop to server, dev to prod, team to team — you rebuild the whole thing. **That's broken.**\n\n**RagBucket fixes this.**\n\nIt packages your entire RAG pipeline — vectors, chunks, config, and runtime metadata — into a single portable `.rag` artifact. Like a model checkpoint, but for retrieval intelligence.\n\n---\n\n## ◈ Introducing `.rag`\n\n<div align=\"center\">\n<img src=\"frontend/img/main.png\" alt=\"RagBucket Architecture\" width=\"800\" />\n</div>\n\n<br/>\n\nA `.rag` artifact is a **self-contained, executable unit of retrieval intelligence.** It is not a config file. It is not a directory. It is a complete, ready-to-run retrieval system.\n\n| What it stores              | How it stores it             |\n| :-------------------------- | :--------------------------- |\n| Semantic embeddings         | via Sentence Transformers    |\n| Vector index                | via FAISS                    |\n| Chunked knowledge           | via LangChain splitters      |\n| Retrieval configuration     | embedded in manifest         |\n| Runtime metadata            | versioned artifact manifest  |\n\n```\nBuild it once.\nDrop it anywhere.\nQuery it with one line of code.\n```\n\n---\n\n## ◈ Full Architecture\n\n<div align=\"center\">\n<img src=\"frontend/img/workflow.png\" alt=\"RagBucket Full Workflow\" width=\"900\" />\n</div>\n\n---\n\n## ◈ Installation\n\n```bash\n# Using uv (recommended)\nuv add ragbucket\n\n# Using pip\npip install ragbucket\n```\n\n> **Lightweight by default.** Local embedding dependencies are only pulled in when you set `embedding_provider=\"local\"`. Cloud providers add nothing to your base install.\n\n---\n\n## ◈ Quickstart\n\n### Step 1 — Build a Portable `.rag` Artifact\n\n```python\nfrom ragbucket import RagBuilder, RagConfig\nimport os\nfrom dotenv import load_dotenv\n\nload_dotenv()\n\nconfig = RagConfig(\n\n    # ── Embedding Provider ────────────────────────────────────\n    embedding_provider = \"cohere\",\n    embedding_model    = \"embed-english-v3.0\",\n    embedding_api_key  = os.getenv(\"COHERE_API_KEY\"),\n\n    # ── Chunking ──────────────────────────────────────────────\n    chunk_size    = 512,\n    chunk_overlap = 50,\n\n    # ── Retrieval ─────────────────────────────────────────────\n    top_k = 3,\n)\n\nbuilder = RagBuilder(config=config)\n\nbuilder.build(\n    doc_path = \"docs/\",\n    op_path  = \"artifacts/demo.rag\",\n)\n```\n\nThis generates a single portable artifact:\n\n```\nartifacts/\n└── demo.rag          ← your entire RAG pipeline, packaged\n```\n\n---\n\n### Step 2 — Load and Query the Artifact\n\n```python\nfrom ragbucket import RagRuntime\nimport os\nfrom dotenv import load_dotenv\n\nload_dotenv()\n\nrag = RagRuntime(\n\n    # ── RAG Artifact ──────────────────────────────────────────\n    rag_path = \"artifacts/demo.rag\",\n\n    # ── Generation Provider ───────────────────────────────────\n    provider = \"groq\",\n    api_key  = os.getenv(\"GROQ_API_KEY\"),\n    model    = \"llama-3.1-8b-instant\",\n\n    # ── Embedding Provider Key ────────────────────────────────\n    embedding_api_key = os.getenv(\"COHERE_API_KEY\"),\n\n    # ── System Prompt ─────────────────────────────────────────\n    system_prompt = \"You are a helpful assistant. Keep answers short and crisp.\",\n)\n\nresponse = rag.ask(\"What are Anik's AI/ML skills?\")\nprint(response)\n```\n\nThat's it. No vector DB to spin up. No pipeline to reconstruct. Just load and ask.\n\n---\n\n## ◈ Multi-Provider Runtime\n\nRagBucket cleanly separates **retrieval** from **generation** — meaning you can mix and match embedding providers with generation providers freely.\n\n### Generation Providers\n\n| Provider      | Example Model                 |\n| :------------ | :---------------------------- |\n| `groq`        | `llama-3.1-8b-instant`        |\n| `openai`      | `gpt-4o-mini`                 |\n| `gemini`      | `gemini-1.5-flash`            |\n| `anthropic`   | `claude-3-haiku-20240307`     |\n\n```python\n# Swap providers without touching anything else\nrag = RagRuntime(\n    rag_path  = \"demo.rag\",\n    provider  = \"anthropic\",\n    api_key   = os.getenv(\"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY\"),\n    model     = \"claude-3-haiku-20240307\",\n    embedding_api_key = os.getenv(\"COHERE_API_KEY\"),\n)\n```\n\n### Embedding Providers\n\n| Provider    | Example Model                       |\n| :---------- | :---------------------------------- |\n| `local`     | `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5`            |\n| `cohere`    | `embed-english-v3.0`                |\n| `openai`    | `text-embedding-3-small`            |\n| `gemini`    | `models/embedding-001`              |\n| `voyage`    | `voyage-large-2`                    |\n\n```python\n# Use any embedding provider at build time\nconfig = RagConfig(\n    embedding_provider = \"openai\",\n    embedding_model    = \"text-embedding-3-small\",\n    embedding_api_key  = os.getenv(\"OPENAI_API_KEY\"),\n)\n```\n\n---\n\n## ◈ Dynamic Retrieval Configuration\n\nEvery stage of the retrieval pipeline is configurable. Sane defaults are always applied automatically.\n\n```python\nfrom ragbucket import RagConfig\n\nconfig = RagConfig(\n\n    # Embedding system\n    embedding_provider = \"local\",\n    embedding_model    = \"sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2\",\n\n    # Chunking\n    chunk_size    = 1024,\n    chunk_overlap = 100,\n\n    # Retrieval\n    top_k = 5,\n)\n```\n\n> All missing values are filled using framework defaults. Nothing breaks if you leave something out.\n\n---\n\n## ◈ What a `.rag` Artifact Contains\n\n```\ndemo.rag\n│\n├── vectors.faiss     ← FAISS vector index (semantic search backbone)\n├── chunks.json       ← document chunks with source metadata\n└── manifest.json     ← embedding config, top_k, model info, version\n```\n\nThe artifact is entirely self-describing. Anyone who receives a `.rag` file has everything needed to query it — no external config, no infrastructure dependencies, no guesswork.\n\n---\n\n## ◈ Technology Stack\n\n| Component           | Technology                  |\n| :------------------ | :-------------------------- |\n| Embeddings          | Sentence Transformers       |\n| Vector Search       | FAISS                       |\n| Chunking            | LangChain Text Splitters    |\n| Artifact Packaging  | Python `zipfile`            |\n| Config Validation   | Pydantic                    |\n| Runtime             | Pure Python                 |\n\n---\n\n## ◈ Philosophy\n\n> *RAG systems should be as portable as model files. Not as fragile as microservice stacks.*\n\nRagBucket treats RAG systems as **portable intelligence artifacts** — not fragile infrastructure pipelines. This cleanly separates two concerns that have no business being coupled:\n\n```\nRetrieval memory   →  what you built      →  lives in the .rag file\nLanguage generation →  how you query it   →  any provider, any environment\n```\n\nYour retrieval knowledge travels with your code. Swap generation providers without rebuilding anything. Share a `.rag` file like you'd share a model checkpoint.\n\nThe result: reusable semantic memory that is fully decoupled from infrastructure.\n\n---\n\n## ◈ Links\n\n| Resource   | URL                                                               |\n| :--------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| Website    | [ragbucket.vercel.app](https://ragbucket.vercel.app)             |\n| PyPI       | [pypi.org/project/ragbucket](https://pypi.org/project/ragbucket) |\n| GitHub     | [github.com/anikchand461/ragbucket](https://github.com/anikchand461/ragbucket) |\n\n---\n\n## ◈ License\n\nMIT License — see [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.\n\n---\n\n<div align=\"center\">\n\n<br/>\n\n```\n◈ RagBucket\n```\n\n*The portable runtime layer for Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems.*\n\nBuilt by [Anik Chand](https://github.com/anikchand461) · [ragbucket.vercel.app](https://ragbucket.vercel.app)\n\n<br/>\n\n</div>\n"

            "path": "ragbucket/builder/indexer.py",
            "content": "# This file defines the vector indexing engine\n# of the RAG pipeline.\n\n# Import FAISS for vector similarity indexing and retrieval\nimport faiss\n\n# Import NumPy for numerical array conversion.\nimport numpy as np\n\n\n# Indexer class responsible for converting embeddings into a searchable FAISS index.\nclass Indexer:\n\n    # Build a FAISS vector index from embeddings.\n    def build_index(self, embedding):\n\n        # Convert embeddings into a NumPy float32 array,\n        # which is required by FAISS.\n        embeddings = np.array(\n            embedding,\n            dtype=\"float32\"\n        )\n\n        # Extract embedding dimensionality.\n        #\n        # Example:\n        # embeddings.shape = (100, 384)\n        #\n        # meaning:\n        # 100 vectors\n        # each vector has 384 dimensions\n        dimension = embeddings.shape[1]\n\n        # Create a flat L2 distance index.\n        #\n        # L2 = Euclidean distance similarity search.\n        index = faiss.IndexFlatL2(dimension)\n        # an empty database table created \n\n        # Add embeddings into the FAISS index.\n        index.add(embeddings)\n        # the embeddings are inserted in the database table \n\n        # Return the searchable vector index.\n        return index\n"

Package all RAG components into a .rag file.\n    def package(self, output_path, index, chunks, manifest):\n\n        # Create a temporary staging directory\n        # used for assembling artifact files.\n        temp_dir = Path(\"temp_rag\")\n\n        # Create the directory if it does not exist.\n        temp_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n\n        # Save the FAISS vector index into the\n        # temporary artifact directory.\n        #\n        # This stores the searchable semantic memory\n        # of the RAG system.\n        faiss.write_index(index, str(temp_dir / \"vectors.faiss\"))\n\n        # Store all chunked document text\n        # inside chunks.json\n        with open(temp_dir / \"chunks.json\", \"w\") as f:\n            json.dump(chunks, f, indent=2)\n\n        # Store artifact metadata and configuration\n        # inside manifest.json\n        with open(temp_dir / \"manifest.json\", \"w\") as f:\n            json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2)\n\n        # Create the final .rag archive.\n        #\n        # ZIP_DEFLATED enables compression\n        # to reduce artifact size.\n        with zipfile.ZipFile(output_path, \"w\", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zipf:\n\n            # Iterate through all generated files\n            # inside the temporary directory.\n            for file in temp_dir.iterdir():\n\n                # Add each file into the .rag archive.\n                #\n                # arcname=file.name ensures that only\n                # clean filenames are stored inside\n                # the artifact instead of full paths.\n                zipf.write(file, arcname=file.name)\n\n        # Display successful artifact creation message.\n        print(f\"\\nCreated {output_path}\")\n"

            "content": "# This file defines the semantic retrieval engine\n# of the runtime pipeline.\n\n\n# Import NumPy for vector conversion.\nimport numpy as np\n\n\n# Import the globally cached embedding model.\nfrom ragbucket.embeddings.factory import get_embedder\n\n\n# Retriever class responsible for:\n# - embedding user queries\n# - performing semantic search\n# - retrieving relevant chunks\nclass Retriever:\n\n    def __init__(self, config: dict):\n        self.config = config\n        self.model = get_embedder(\n            provider=config[\"embedding_provider\"],\n            model=config[\"embedding_model\"],\n            api_key=config.get(\"embedding_api_key\")\n        )\n\n    # Retrieve the most relevant chunks\n    # for a given user query.\n    def retrieve(\n        self,\n        query: str,\n        index,\n        chunks,\n        top_k = None\n    ):\n\n        if top_k is None:\n            top_k = self.config[\"top_k\"]\n\n        # Convert the user query into\n        # a semantic vector embedding.\n        query_embedding = self.model.embed(\n            [query]\n        )\n\n        # Convert embeddings into float32 format\n        # required by FAISS.\n        query_embedding = np.array(\n            query_embedding,\n            dtype=\"float32\"\n        )\n\n        # Perform semantic similarity search.\n        #\n        # Returns:\n        # - distances\n        # - matching indices\n        distances, indices = index.search(\n            query_embedding,\n            top_k\n        )\n\n        # Retrieve matching chunks using\n        # the returned indices.\n        retrieved_chunks = [\n            chunks[i]\n            for i in indices[0]\n        ]\n\n        return retrieved_chunks\n"

            "content": "from ragbucket.runtime.loader import RagLoader\nfrom ragbucket.runtime.retriever import Retriever\nfrom ragbucket.runtime.providers.factory import get_provider\n\nclass RagRuntime:\n\n    def __init__(self, rag_path, provider, api_key, model, embedding_api_key=None, system_prompt=None):\n\n        loader = RagLoader()\n        loaded = loader.load(rag_path)\n\n        self.index = loaded[\"index\"]\n        self.chunks = loaded[\"chunks\"]\n        self.manifest = loaded[\"manifest\"]\n        self.config = self.manifest[\"config\"]\n\n        if embedding_api_key is not None:\n            self.config[\"embedding_api_key\"] = embedding_api_key\n\n        self.retriever = Retriever(config=self.config)\n        self.generator = get_provider(\n            provider=provider,\n            api_key=api_key,\n            model=model\n        )\n        self.system_prompt = system_prompt\n\n    def ask(self, query):\n        retrieved_chunks = self.retriever.retrieve(\n            query = query,\n            index = self.index,\n            chunks = self.chunks\n        )\n\n        answer = self.generator.generate(\n            query = query,\n            context = retrieved_chunks,\n            system_prompt = self.system_prompt\n        )\n\n        return answer\n"

--- ## 🩺 What is MediBot? **MediBot** is a polite, conversational AI medical assistant built with **Streamlit**
and powered by **Groq's LLaMA 3.1 8B** model via **LangChain**.
It listens to your health concerns and offers calm, concise, practical advice —
like having a knowledgeable friend on call, anytime.
> ⚠️ MediBot is an informational assistant only. It does **not** replace professional medical advice.
Always consult a licensed healthcare provider for serious concerns. ## ✨ Features | Feature | Description | |:---:|:---| | 💬 **Conversational Memory** | Full multi-turn chat — MediBot remembers your conversation context | | 🧠 **LLM-Powered** | Backed by `llama-3.1-8b-instant` via Groq for fast, intelligent responses | | 🎯 **Medical Focus** | Politely redirects off-topic queries back to health-related discussions | | ⚡ **Real-time Streaming UI** | Clean chat bubbles with a responsive Streamlit interface | | 🔄 **Session Management** | Clear chat anytime via the sidebar | | 🔒 **Secure Key Handling** | API keys loaded via `.env` locally or `st.secrets` on deployment | --- ## 🖼️ Preview ``` ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ 🤖 MediBot │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ │ │ ╭──────────────────────────────────────────╮ │ │ │ Hello, I am a medical assistant. │ 🤖 │ │ │ How can I help you? │ │ │ ╰──────────────────────────────────────────╯ │ │ │ │ ╭──────────────────────────────────╮ │ │ 👤 │ I have a fever and a headache. │ │ │ ╰──────────────────────────────────╯ │ │ │ │ ╭──────────────────────────────────────────╮ │ │ │ For fever and headache, Paracetamol can │ 🤖 │ │ │ help relieve both symptoms. │ │ │ ╰──────────────────────────────────────────╯ │ │ │ │ [ Type your message... ] [Send] │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` --- ## 🚀 Getting Started ### Prerequisites Python 3.10+  |  A [Groq API key](https://console.groq.com/) *(free tier available)*
### 1️⃣ Clone the Repository ```bash git clone https://github.com/shreya/medibot.git cd medibot ``` ### 2️⃣ Install Dependencies ```bash pip install -r requirements.txt ``` ### 3️⃣ Set Up Environment Variables ```env GROQ_API_KEY=your_groq_api_key_here ``` ### 4️⃣ Run the App ```bash streamlit run app.py ``` Visit `http://localhost:8501` in your browser — MediBot is live! 🎉 --- ## 📁 Project Structure ``` medibot/ │ ├── app.py # Streamlit UI — chat interface, session state, styling ├── main.py # LangChain + Groq LLM integration, get_response() ├── .env # Local secrets (not committed) ├── requirements.txt └── README.md ``` --- ## 🛠️ Tech Stack ``` Frontend → Streamlit (chat UI, session state, sidebar controls) LLM → Groq API (llama-3.1-8b-instant — ultra-fast inference) Orchestration → LangChain (SystemMessage / HumanMessage / AIMessage) Secrets → python-dotenv + st.secrets (local + cloud) ``` --- ## ⚙️ How It Works ``` User types a message │ ▼ app.py appends message to session_state.messages │ ▼ get_response(messages) called in main.py │ ▼ LangChain formats the full conversation history ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐ │ SystemMessage (MediBot persona) │ │ HumanMessage (user turn 1) │ │ AIMessage (bot turn 1) │ │ HumanMessage (user turn 2) │ │ ... │ └─────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ Groq LLaMA 3.1 8B generates a response │ ▼ Reply is trimmed and displayed in the chat UI ``` --- ## 🌐 Deployment (Streamlit Cloud) **1.** Push your code to a **public GitHub repository**
**2.** Go to [streamlit.io/cloud](https://streamlit.io/cloud) and connect your repo
**3.** In **App Settings → Secrets**, add: ```toml GROQ_API_KEY = "your_groq_api_key_here" ``` **4.** Deploy! Your app will be live at `https://your-app.streamlit.app` 🚀 --- ## 📦 Requirements ```txt streamlit groq python-dotenv langchain-groq ``` --- ## 🤝 Contributing Contributions are welcome! Feel free to open an issue or submit a pull request. **1.** Fork the repository
**2.** Create your feature branch — `git checkout -b feature/amazing-feature`
**3.** Commit your changes — `git commit -m 'Add amazing feature'`
**4.** Push to the branch — `git push origin feature/amazing-feature`
**5.** Open a Pull Request --- ## 📄 License This project is open source and available under the [MIT License](LICENSE). ---

def github_get(endpoint, params=None, github_token=None):
    headers = deepcopy(HEADERS)

    if github_token:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {github_token}"
        print("AUTH: using token")
    else:
        print("AUTH: NO TOKEN")

    response = requests.get(
        BASE_URL + endpoint,
        headers=headers,
        params=params,
    )

    print("URL:", BASE_URL + endpoint)
    print("Status:", response.status_code)
    print("Remaining:", response.headers.get("X-RateLimit-Remaining"))

    if not response.ok:
        print("Response:", response.text)

    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()

import base64
from urllib.parse import quote

from .client import github_get
from .tree import get_tree


SOURCE_EXTENSIONS = (
    ".py",
    ".js",
    ".ts",
    ".tsx",
    ".java",
    ".cpp",
    ".c",
    ".go",
    ".rs",
    ".php",
    ".html",
    ".css",
    ".json",
    ".md",
    ".yml",
    ".yaml",
)


def get_file(owner, repo, path, branch=None, github_token=None):
    path = quote(path, safe="/")

    params = {}

    if branch:
        params["ref"] = branch

    data = github_get(
        f"/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}",
        params=params,
        github_token=github_token,
    )

    if data.get("type") != "file":
        return None

    content = base64.b64decode(
        data["content"]
    ).decode(
        "utf-8",
        errors="ignore",
    )

    return {
        "path": path,
        "content": content,
    }


def get_all_files(owner, repo, branch=None, github_token=None):
    tree = get_tree(
        owner,
        repo,
        branch,
        github_token=github_token,
    )

    files = []

    for item in tree:
        if item["type"] != "blob":
            continue

        path = item["path"]

        if path.endswith(SOURCE_EXTENSIONS):
            file = get_file(
                owner,
                repo,
                path,
                branch,
                github_token=github_token,
            )

            if file:
                files.append(file)

    return files
